content.value_statement: Shell scripts often fail from quoting errors, portability gaps, and weak CI linting. This skill guides ShellCheck setup, rule handling, and workflow integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains ShellCheck installation paths for Homebrew, Debian packages, source builds, and version checks.
Shows project .shellcheckrc options for target shells, enabled checks, disabled rules, and external sources.
Guides CI integration for local hooks, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and failure behavior.
Maps common ShellCheck warnings to practical fixes for quoting, portability, and exit checks.
Describes output formats for terminal review, CI annotations, quiet checks, and parser integrations.
limitations: Does not execute ShellCheck or inspect files without user-provided project context.
Does not replace manual review for complex shell behavior or production deployment risk.
Examples require adaptation for each operating system, package manager, and CI environment.
Suppression guidance can hide real defects if teams do not document rule exceptions.

use_cases.title: Add CI ShellCheck Gate
use_cases.description: Configure ShellCheck in CI so shell scripts fail builds when lint errors appear.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Rules
use_cases.description: Create a .shellcheckrc policy that matches supported shells and approved exclusions.

use_cases.title: Review Script Quality
use_cases.description: Interpret ShellCheck warnings before deployment and prioritize fixes for risky shell patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic Linting
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me install ShellCheck and run it on a Bash script. Explain each setup step and how to verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .shellcheckrc for a project that supports Bash and POSIX sh. Include rule choices and reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate ShellCheck in CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a ShellCheck workflow for our repository. Include local hooks, CI behavior, output format, and failure rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Suppressions and Portability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our ShellCheck exclusions and script portability goals. Identify risky suppressions and recommend safer rule settings.

output_examples.input: A team wants ShellCheck added before pull requests merge.
output: Recommended CI gate and local hook approach.
Shell dialect setting for the repository.
Failure policy and reviewer notes for suppressions.

output_examples.input: A script reports quoting and exit-code warnings.
A project has many disabled ShellCheck rules.
output_examples.output: A suppression review that separates justified exclusions from risky blanket disables.

best_practices: Set the target shell explicitly before interpreting warnings.
Document every disabled ShellCheck rule with a clear project reason.
Run ShellCheck both locally and in CI before release.
anti_patterns: Disabling broad rule groups without reviewing the affected scripts.
Treating ShellCheck output as optional after adding it to CI.
Copying installation commands into production hosts without package review.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure ShellCheck rules, output formats, CI checks, and suppression policies for shell scripts.

faq.question: Can it explain ShellCheck warning codes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common warning codes and connects them to safer shell script patterns.

faq.question: Does it run ShellCheck automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. The user must choose when to run commands.

faq.question: Can it support POSIX sh and Bash?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers target shell settings for Bash, POSIX sh, dash, and related shells.

faq.question: How should teams handle false positives?
faq.answer: Teams should document each suppression and review disabled rules during code review.

faq.question: Is it useful for CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and pre-commit checks.
